rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a visual picture or image, including a printed or digital one.

example.english: This picture is one I took yesterday.
example.traditional: 呢張圖片係我尋日影嘅。
example.jyutping: ni1 zoeng1 tou4 pin2 hai6 ngo5 cam4 jat6 jeng2 ge3

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb for imagining or envisioning something.

example.traditional: 我可以想像到嗰個畫面。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ho2 ji5 soeng2 zoeng6 dou3 go2 go3 waa6 min6

rows.note: Use this for representing someone or something visually by drawing it.

example.english: I’ll draw a picture of your whole family.
example.jyutping: ngo5 bong1 nei5 waa2 fuk1 cyun4 gaa1 fuk1

rows.note: Use this when “picture” means to describe something vividly in words rather than draw it.

example.english: They picture the scene very vividly.
example.traditional: 佢哋將個場面形容得好生動。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 zoeng1 go3 coeng4 min6 jing4 jung4 dak1 hou2 sang1 dung6

rows.note: Use this when “picture” means cinema or films as entertainment rather than a still image.

example.english: We’re going to see a picture tonight.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 gam1 maan5 heoi3 tai2 din6 jing2

rows.note: Use this for a picture formed in the mind or an imagined visual scene.

example.english: I can still picture the scene he described.
example.traditional: 佢講到嗰個畫面，我而家仲記得。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gong2 dou3 go2 go3 waa6 min6 ngo5 ji4 gaa1 zung6 gei3 dak1

rows.note: Use this for a person or thing presented as a perfect model of a category.

example.english: She is a picture of professional excellence in the industry.
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 jip6 gaai3 gung1 jan6 ge3 din2 faan6
